title: Search a sorted sample table
description: Implement int lower_bound_sample(const int* values, std::size_t n, int target).
prompt:
Implement int lower_bound_sample(const int* values, std::size_t n, int target).
Return the first index whose value is at least target, or n when no such index exists. The array is sorted in nondecreasing order.
constraints: values may be nullptr when n is zero.
Use O(log n) comparisons and O(1) additional memory.

reference_solution.solution.cpp:
#include "window.hpp"
int lower_bound_sample(const int* v,std::size_t n,int target){std::size_t lo=0,hi=n;while(lo<hi){auto m=lo+(hi-lo)/2;if(v[m]<target)lo=m+1;else hi=m;}return static_cast<int>(lo);}

rubric: Respect the stated contract and bounds.
Explain integer widths, ownership, and relevant edge cases.
Separate host-test evidence from hardware guarantees.
follow_ups: Do passing functional tests establish logarithmic complexity?
What if DMA can modify the table while it is being searched?
hints: Write down the boundary cases before choosing an implementation.
